newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Spain to forgive $525 mln in Guatemalan debt.
newsitem.headline: Spain to forgive $525 mln in Guatemalan debt.

text.p: Spain has agreed to accept $125 million in payments to cancel a $650 million, 15-year-old debt that Guatemala owes a Spanish bank on a loan for a failed paper pulp plant, a diplomat said Monday.

"The debt will be reduced, according to an agreement, from $650 million to $125 million, with the promise of an immediate payment of $5 million," Juan Jose Serra, Guatemala's ambassador to Mexico, told Reuters through a spokesman.

Serra was in Spain this month to negotiate with the Spanish government regarding a loan from Spain's Banco Exterior to Celulose of Guatemala, a defunct company owned by a group of Spanish and Guatemalan investors.

In 1981, Guatemala's state-owned National Financing Corporation, an agency for development projects, guaranteed a $188 million loan for the construction of Celgusa's pulp- producing plant. Celulose built the plant, which shut down before ever operating. No payments were ever made on the loan.
Serra said as the debt mounted by $2 million a month over more than a decade, it soured commercial relations with Spain and strained Guatemala's relations with the Paris Club.
Under the new agreement, Guatemala has 25 years to pay off the debt, with a five-year grace period.
Serra said Spain will give Guatemala $8 million in foreign aid each year for three years and also will loan Guatemala $150,000 for development projects.
